title: Value of a linear Boolean function on an indicator vector
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a linear Boolean function, meaning $f(x \oplus y) = f(x) \oplus f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$, where $\oplus$ is componentwise XOR. For a subset $s \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $\mathbf{1}_s \in \{0,1\}^n$ be its indicator vector, whose $i$-th coordinate is $1$ when $i \in s$ and $0$ otherwise, and for each index $i$ let $e_i \in \{0,1\}^n$ be the standard basis vector, whose $i$-th coordinate is $1$ and all others $0$. Then for every $s$ the value $f(\mathbf{1}_s)$ is $0$ when
\[
  \sum_{i \in s} \mathbf{1}[\,f(e_i) = 1\,] \equiv 0 \pmod 2,
\]
and $1$ otherwise; that is, $f(\mathbf{1}_s)$ equals the parity of the number of $i \in s$ with $f(e_i) = 1$.

replaced:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be linear.  Then for every
$s \subseteq [n]$, writing $\mathbf{1}_s$ for the indicator vector of $s$ and
$e_i$ for the $i$-th basis vector, the value $f(\mathbf{1}_s)$ is
\texttt{false} when
\[
  \sum_{i \in s} \mathbf{1}[f(e_i) = \texttt{true}] \equiv 0 \pmod 2
\]
and \texttt{true} otherwise; that is, $f(\mathbf{1}_s)$ is the parity of the
number of $i \in s$ with $f(e_i) = \texttt{true}$.
